messages:
alexa: quick heads-up, after landing kernel-selector-v3 we see a p99 tail regression on streaming chat canary (was stable before).
ben: numbers?
alexa: streaming canary (mb=3) p95 ~ 78ms, p99 ~ 640ms, tail >1s ~0.9% of requests. non-streaming completions (mb=10) p95 ~ 240ms, p99 ~ 1.1s — the completions tail is higher but within expected throughput tradeoffs.
carla: wow, streaming p99 is really spiking. did anything touch KV cache or memory layout?
alexa: profiler shows KV hit rate dropped 90% -> 58% after the selector flip. evictions went way up. suspect the new kernel moves KV buf to larger aligned pages and our eviction accounting misses that.
dmitri: can you paste the profiler summary?
alexa: ```
KVCache: capacity=140k -> active=98k
evictions/min: 200 -> 4200
kv_hit_rate: 0.90 -> 0.58
kv_reads/sec: 1800 -> 6200
kernel_choice: baseline_attn -> optimized_attn_v3
latency_tail_samples: 820ms, 1.8s, 3.1s
```
ben: optimized_attn_v3 pins buffers differently. combined with microbatch scheduling (partial fill + preempt) that could amplify tail. for streaming small mb is preferred.
carla: agree. streaming workloads should bias towards mb<=2 to cap handshake/tail. can we run an mb=2 streaming canary with the old kernel hint for hot sessions?
alexa: launched mb=2 streaming canary + kernel_hint=legacy-hot. Warm numbers after 20m: streaming p95 ~ 72ms, p99 ~ 150ms. eviction rates down ~70%.
ben: good. cost/throughput impact?
alexa: GPU kernels run slightly more often, throughput down ~12% for streaming but overall cost +3% which looks acceptable to meet SLO.
dmitri: longer term we should: 1) fix eviction to be aware of pinned/aligned buffers, 2) add KV prefetch hysteresis (only prefetch for sessions with >1 turn in 1s window), 3) router heuristic to cap mb for streaming.
carla: +1. propose router rule: if request.client_type == "streaming" OR has_stream_flag -> mb_max=2, else allow autotuner up to mb=16. seed autotuner with this rule.
alexa: quick AB: applied router rule in warm canary. streaming p99 ~140ms, completions unchanged, overall tail mass back to baseline.
deploybot: deploybot: Canary rollout (kernel-selector-v3) finished for canary group (5/5). monitor: https://deploys.redwood/rollouts/2317
ben: catalogue follow-ups: (A) INF-4999 kernel->kv interaction: attach profiler dumps (alexa), (B) router mb heuristic PR (carla), (C) eviction/alloc fix prototype (dmitri), (D) add eviction_rate metric to runtime dashboard + alert (>2x baseline).
alexa: filed INF-4999 and attached traces (trace_id=omega-1751111001).
carla: I'll open the router PR today, target review by EOD.
dmitri: prototyping eviction accounting now; will simulate with pinned allocations and run hit-rate regression.
ben: make sure we track both p95 SLOs (streaming target p95 <120ms) and completion p95 (<260ms) during rollout. also run a longer 6h canary before stable rollout.
alexa: TL;DR: kernel-selector change exposed mismatch with KV eviction & pinned buffer layout => streaming p99 spike. Immediate mitigation: cap streaming microbatch to 2 + kernel hint for hot sessions. Follow-ups in INF-4999.
